source.sql:
-- Executed growth bridge with a window function. New/returning revenue uses
-- known IDs only; gross_sales and net_sales above retain anonymous shoppers.
WITH first_purchase AS (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(SUBSTR(invoice_date, 1, 7)) AS first_month
    FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_mix AS (
    SELECT SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7) AS month,
           SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7) = f.first_month THEN o.revenue ELSE 0 END) AS first_observed_customer_revenue,
           SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7) > f.first_month THEN o.revenue ELSE 0 END) AS returning_customer_revenue
    FROM orders o JOIN first_purchase f USING (customer_id)
    WHERE o.invoice_date >= :period_start AND o.invoice_date < :period_end
    GROUP BY SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7)
),
growth AS (
    SELECT month, gross_sales, returns_value, net_sales, orders, customers,
           LAG(net_sales) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS previous_month_net_sales
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT g.*, (g.net_sales - g.previous_month_net_sales) / NULLIF(g.previous_month_net_sales, 0) AS net_sales_mom,
       c.first_observed_customer_revenue, c.returning_customer_revenue,
       c.returning_customer_revenue / NULLIF(c.first_observed_customer_revenue + c.returning_customer_revenue, 0) AS returning_customer_revenue_share
FROM growth g LEFT JOIN customer_mix c USING (month)
ORDER BY month;

source.sql:
SELECT country,
       SUM(line_revenue) AS gross_sales,
       COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_no) AS orders,
       COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers
FROM line_items
WHERE kind = 'sale' AND invoice_date >= :period_start AND invoice_date < :period_end
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY gross_sales DESC, country;

source.sql:
-- First OBSERVED purchase cohorts, not proven acquisition cohorts: the source
-- contains no pre-December-2010 purchase history. Generate only mature cells.
WITH RECURSIVE
customer_first AS (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(SUBSTR(invoice_date, 1, 7)) AS cohort
    FROM orders WHERE invoice_date < :period_end GROUP BY customer_id
),
cohort_sizes AS (
    SELECT cohort, COUNT(*) AS cohort_size FROM customer_first GROUP BY cohort
),
ages(age_month) AS (
    SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT age_month + 1 FROM ages WHERE age_month < 120
),
mature_grid AS (
    SELECT s.cohort, a.age_month, s.cohort_size,
           STRFTIME('%Y-%m', DATE(s.cohort || '-01', '+' || a.age_month || ' months')) AS activity_month
    FROM cohort_sizes s CROSS JOIN ages a
    WHERE DATE(s.cohort || '-01', '+' || a.age_month || ' months') < DATE(:period_end)
),
activity AS (
    SELECT f.cohort, SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7) AS activity_month,
           COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customers
    FROM orders o JOIN customer_first f USING (customer_id)
    WHERE o.invoice_date < :period_end
    GROUP BY f.cohort, SUBSTR(o.invoice_date, 1, 7)
)
SELECT g.cohort, g.age_month, COALESCE(a.customers, 0) AS customers,
       g.cohort_size, 1.0 * COALESCE(a.customers, 0) / g.cohort_size AS retention
FROM mature_grid g LEFT JOIN activity a
  ON g.cohort = a.cohort AND g.activity_month = a.activity_month
ORDER BY g.cohort, g.age_month;

model.target: At least one valid positive purchase in the next 30 days
limitations: One historical retailer with wholesalers; no modern-market generalization is established.
Customer IDs excluded from predictors; known customers may recur across temporal windows.
November seasonality may shift purchase rates. Bootstrap intervals exclude time-period uncertainty.
Purchase propensity is not treatment uplift. No campaign assignment, cost or margin is observed.
Priority is a value-times-nonpurchase heuristic, not an experimentally validated optimal policy.
Order value is historical gross positive invoice value, capped at training P95; returns and margin are not learned.
